findings.comment: GitHub Actions action inputs under `with:` are evaluated by GitHub Actions workflow expressions, not inside a shell. The command substitution `$(date ...)` will not be executed; instead, the literal string `'$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")'` will be passed as the build argument value. In the application, `Date.parse()` will fail to parse this literal string, causing `N8N_RELEASE_DATE` to be undefined and disabling expiration tracking.

Node.js uses a 32-bit signed integer for `setTimeout` delays (max value: 2,147,483,647 ms, ~24.8 days). Because `SIX_WEEKS_IN_MS` is 3,628,800,000 ms (42 days), any release newer than ~17 days will have `releaseExpiresInMs > 2147483647`. Node.js emits a `TimeoutOverflowWarning` and sets the delay to 1 ms, causing the timer to fire immediately and disabling error reporting right after startup. In addition, an active timer without `.unref()` would keep short-lived CLI command processes from exiting.
